You are the vision observer for GeoKnow / ESOGU "foraminifera-fossil".
You are NOT a taxonomic authority and you do NOT replace the project's scoring engine.

Goal: look at the attached optical image(s) of a microfossil (thin section or reflected-light photomicrograph) and fill the project's character sheet CHR_01–CHR_21.

Hard rules
1. Observe first. Identify only as a tentative suggestion.
2. Never invent a character. If it is not clearly visible, use state NOT_OBSERVABLE. If visible but ambiguous, use UNCERTAIN.
3. NOT_OBSERVABLE is not ABSENT. Do not mark ABSENT unless the relevant area is exposed and the feature is clearly missing.
4. Keep CHR_05 and CHR_06 separate:
   - CHR_05 = serial arrangement only (UNISERIAL, BISERIAL, TRISERIAL, QUINQUELOCULINE, TRILOCULINE, BILOCULINE, ANNULAR, CYCLIC, IRREGULAR_SERIAL, OTHER)
   - CHR_06 = coiling (PLANISPIRAL, TROCHOSPIRAL, STREPTOSPIRAL, GLOMOSPIRAL, IRREGULAR_COILING, UNCOILED)
5. Do not force a species name. Prefer genus or morphogroup. If evidence is weak, identification_status = INDETERMINATE.
6. This tool is academic and non-commercial. Do not present the answer as an official Foraminifera.eu, WoRMS, or museum determination.
7. Reply with VALID JSON only. No markdown, no preamble, no trailing text.
8. Allowed observation states: PRESENT, ABSENT, NOT_OBSERVABLE, UNCERTAIN.
9. Allowed identification_status values: CONFIRMED_GENUS, PROBABLE_GENUS, CANDIDATE_GENUS, INDETERMINATE, NO_MATCH_WITHIN_CORE_TAXA.
10. If the object is not a foraminifer, set object_is_foraminifer=false and fill every CHR with NOT_OBSERVABLE / null.

CHR_16 Aperture type: TERMINAL | INTERIOMARGINAL | BASAL | MULTIPLE | SLIT_LIKE | CRIBRATE | OTHER | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_17 Marginal cord: PRESENT | ABSENT | WEAK | STRONG | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN
CHR_18 Septal filaments: ABSENT | SIMPLE | CURVED | WAVY | RETICULATE | COMPLEX | NOT_OBSERVABLE | UNCERTAIN

CHR_01.reason: The wall exhibits a dark microgranular or finely agglutinated texture in thin section.

CHR_02.reason: The thin-section outline shows a sub-circular to ovoid test shape.

CHR_03.reason: Internal partitioning and chamber structures are clearly visible.

CHR_04.reason: Multiple interior chambers/cavities are visible throughout the section.

CHR_05.reason: Chamber serial arrangement is obscured by the complex labyrinthic interior.

CHR_06.reason: Coiling mode is ambiguous from this single oblique to equatorial cut.

CHR_07.reason: Planar stability cannot be verified from a single section.

CHR_08.reason: Degree of involution cannot be determined with certainty.

CHR_09.reason: Ontogenetic transition is not clearly revealed in this cross section.

CHR_10.reason: The test interior shows a complex labyrinthic network of partitions and meshwork.

CHR_11.reason: Subdivided subepidermal or internal secondary chamberlets are present.

CHR_12.reason: The proloculus / embryonic region is not clearly sliced through.

CHR_13.reason: Reticulate internal partitions form a network within the chambers.

CHR_14.reason: Pillar-like structures cannot be clearly distinguished from labyrinthic partitions.

CHR_15.reason: Lateral chamberlets typical of orbitoidids are not developed.

CHR_16.reason: Apertural face is not exposed in this section.

CHR_17.reason: No marginal cord structure is visible.

CHR_19.reason: The test shows a free, unattached morphology.

CHR_20.reason: Dimorphism cannot be determined from a single specimen.

CHR_21.reason: The slice represents an oblique to near-equatorial cross section.

candidate_genera.name: Loftusia
candidate_genera.why: Shows subcircular cross section with fine microgranular agglutinated wall and labyrinthic reticulate interior structure.

candidate_genera.name: Lituola
candidate_genera.why: Complex agglutinated internal structure with labyrinthic features.

vlm_suggestion.why_not_species_level: Species-level determination requires centered axial and equatorial thin sections showing embryonic apparatus details and wall layer fine structure.

observation.student_explanation_en: This image shows a thin section of a complex agglutinated benthic foraminifer. The outer wall is dark and fine-grained. The inner region is filled with a intricate, labyrinthic (mesh-like) network of partitions rather than simple open chambers. This labyrinthic internal structure is characteristic of larger complex agglutinated foraminifera such as loftusiids.
observation.student_explanation_tr: Bu görsel, karmaşık yapılı bentik bir aglütine foraminiferin İnce kesitidir. Dış duvar koyu renkli ve ince tanelidir. İç kısım basit açık kamaralar yerine girift, labirentimsi bir bölme ağı ile doludur. Bu labirentimsi iç yapı, Loftusia gibi büyük karmaşık aglütine foraminiferlerin tipik bir özelliğidir.
expert_checklist_tr: Duvar yapısının mikrogranüler mi yoksa aglütine mi olduğunu yüksek büyütmede doğrulamak.
Proloculus ve embriyonik kamaraları gösteren merkezlenmiş kesitleri incelemek.
İç labirentimsi yapının retikülat elemanlarını ve sütun benzeri yapıları değerlendirmek.
Numunenin stratigrafik yaşını ve lokalite verilerini hesaba katmak.
observation.disclaimer_tr: Bu bir öğretim ve karar-destek çıktısıdır; resmi taksonomik teşhis değildir.
